name: Improper Authentication
principle: The product accepts a claimed identity without proving, or without sufficiently proving, that the actor is that identity. This lets attackers assume identities, reach protected resources, or execute privileged functionality.
detection_signals: grantAccess(), login(), or admin handler gated by request.getParameter("authenticated"), request.getParameter("user"), Cookie("loggedIn"), or client-supplied role
protected servlet/controller/route lacks @PreAuthorize, @RolesAllowed, @Secured, auth middleware, or explicit authenticate(request) before sensitive action
hard-coded credential comparison such as strcmp(password,"admin") == 0 or password.equals("secret")
partial or flawed credential check such as strncmp(input, stored, 4) == 0, startsWith(), substring(), or inverted boolean result
custom X509TrustManager.checkServerTrusted() empty, HostnameVerifier returns true, CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER=0, or SSL_VERIFY_NONE
password reset or login token generated with rand(), java.util.Random, currentTimeMillis(), sequential IDs, or reusable tokens
login failure path returns without counter, rate limiter, lockout, backoff, or MFA challenge update
negative_signals: Spring Security or equivalent config maps sensitive routes with .authenticated(), @PreAuthorize("isAuthenticated()"), @RolesAllowed, or authenticated middleware
server-side session/security context is created only after PasswordEncoder.matches(), BCrypt.checkpw(), Argon2 verify, or framework authentication succeeds
authorization decision uses server-side principal/session/JWT signature verification, not request parameter or unsigned cookie state
failed login handler updates rate limiter, failed-attempt counter, lockout, backoff, or MFA verification state
TLS client uses default TrustManagerFactory/PKIX validation and hostname verification such as SSL_set1_host or default HTTPS HostnameVerifier
password reset uses high-entropy SecureRandom token, single-use storage, expiration time, and server-side account binding
false_defense_traps: Client-side hidden fields, cookies, or JavaScript checks for authenticated=true are forgeable.
A signed-looking JWT is not authentication if the signature, issuer, audience, and expiration are not verified.
TLS is insufficient when certificate chain or hostname verification is disabled.
CAPTCHA without rate limiting or lockout does not prevent credential stuffing or online guessing.
Strong login can be bypassed by weak password reset, backup API, debug endpoint, or alternate channel.
verification_focus: Does every identity-sensitive entry point prove the actor's identity on the server with an unbypassable and sufficiently strong mechanism?

consequence_chains.trigger: critical function endpoint has no server-side authentication check
client accepts unvalidated or wrong-host TLS certificate
consequence_chains.consequence: attacker impersonates a trusted service and captures credentials or data

consequence_chains.trigger: login accepts unlimited guesses without throttling or lockout
consequence_chains.consequence: attacker brute-forces or stuffs credentials to assume identity

consequence_chains.trigger: password recovery token or challenge is guessable or reusable
consequence_chains.consequence: attacker resets victim credentials and takes over account

patch_principle: Use a vetted authentication framework or platform identity provider instead of custom authentication logic.
Enforce server-side authentication on every protected route, API, admin function, and alternate channel.
Store and verify credentials with strong password hashing and constant framework APIs; remove hard-coded/default credentials.
Add MFA where appropriate and enforce failed-attempt throttling, lockout, backoff, or risk-based challenges.
Use high-entropy single-use recovery tokens and validate TLS certificate chains and hostnames.
